review: skeptic - claims and framing lens, round 2 (reverse_zero_r2)
scope: commits 9e6705e..7bc2688 on branch loop/reverse-zero, worktree /mnt/disks/disk-socrateai-local-1/dualscale-wt-reverse, files under audit/reverse_zero_r2/{registration,X1-cmb,X2-cosmic-web,X3-pta,X4-bao-cmb-sn}
method: Independently re-ran every grep-F command recorded for a declared quote (x4_results.json quotes_verbatim block, X1 planckGmuBound line): all 22 pass. Separately swept the three hand-written Markdown files (X3-pta/README.md, X2-cosmic-web/REPORT.md, X4-bao-cmb-sn/X4_RESULT.md) for quotation-mark spans NOT already registered as a checked quote, and grep -F'd each against the source file it names. Independently reproduced key numeric results (X1 WMAP/SMICA p-values and p_corr, X2 gate chi2/threshold/sigma, X4 CPL-vs-Lambda and M0-vs-Lambda sigma via scipy) against the committed JSON. Verified commit ancestry (registration 9e6705e is an ancestor of every experiment commit), verified nothing was pushed (origin/loop/reverse-zero is still at 8e90996), verified every commit touches only audit/reverse_zero_r2/**, verified LeanMaster's true HEAD (64f905f, v3.28.0) and re-ran a full-tree prohibited-term search there.

violations.quote_as_written: Per the registered decision rule ("Gate fails: no p-values / no bound is reported"), **X3 reports no bound at this amplitude.**
violations.finding: The quoted string is a spliced composite, not a verbatim span of any single source field, presented as if it were X3's own 'registered decision rule'. 'Gate fails: no p-values' is a paraphrase of registration.json tests.X1.decision_rule.if_gate_fails ('No p-values. M0 outcome: NOT TESTED.') -- a DIFFERENT test's rule, not X3's. 'no bound is reported' is a genuine fragment, but of tests.X3.calibration_gates.covariance_check ('...otherwise the covariance is flagged and no bound is reported.'), not of tests.X3.decision_rule (the field actually named 'decision rule', which reads: "Report |c4| < x at 95% (x from the Fieller interval) as a bound, or 'no bound', or ABSENT. M0 (c4 = 0) is 'consistent with' the data iff 0 lies inside the interval. No statement that M0 or K3xT2 predicts c4."). `grep -F -- 'Gate fails: no p-values / no bound is reported' audit/reverse_zero_r2/registration/registration.json` returns no match. This is the ground-rule-7 failure mode named explicitly in the ground rules ('never paraphrase inside quotation marks'), here compounded by attributing text from one test (X1) to another (X3).
violations.consequence: Does not change X3's own numeric result or its CONDITIONAL/no-unconditional-bound verdict, which is independently supported by the actual (correctly quoted elsewhere) decision_rule text and the two amplitude runs. The defect is in how the rule is cited, not in the computation.

violations.quote_as_written: No pulsar subset was named in the registration beyond "14 frequencies, gamma=13/3, fixed noise", so this criterion is this script's own, stated explicitly.
violations.finding: Not a verbatim substring of registration.json. `grep -F -- '14 frequencies, gamma=13/3, fixed noise' audit/reverse_zero_r2/registration/registration.json` returns no match. The actual field (tests.X3.statistic.estimator) reads '...with fixed per-pulsar noise from the release, spectrum gamma = 13/3, first 14 frequencies 1/T..14/T (chosen a priori; 10 and 30 frequencies reported as informational variants only).' -- different word order and wording ('gamma = 13/3' with spaces, not 'gamma=13/3'; no contiguous 'fixed noise' at the end). The phrase as written more closely resembles the outside orchestrator's own paraphrase of the registration passed into this workflow's task text, not the frozen registration.json file itself -- i.e. rule 7 names the wrong / an unverifiable source.
violations.consequence: The underlying substantive claim (registration does not name a pulsar subset beyond gamma=13/3, fixed noise, 14 frequencies) is true in substance, confirmed by reading the actual field; only the quotation-mark treatment is wrong.

violations.quote_as_written: it reads as "disfavoured relative to fitted Lambda at that DR2 + compressed-CMB combination" (registration's own phrasing for this case), still **not a P1 verdict**.
violations.finding: Explicitly claimed as 'registration's own phrasing' but is not a substring of registration.json anywhere. `grep -F -- "compressed-CMB combination" audit/reverse_zero_r2/registration/registration.json` returns no match; registration.json's X4 entry uses 'compressed CMB (distance priors)' and 'compressed CMB distance priors', never this exact phrase or sentence. The sentence is the author's own composed wording, mislabeled as a registration quote.
violations.consequence: Substantive framing (M0 vs Lambda disfavoured at 2.16-2.17 sigma, not a P1 verdict, DR2 is not one of P1's named datasets) is otherwise correct and separately, correctly stated without quote marks elsewhere in the same file (e.g. line 8-14). Only this one sentence wrongly dresses invented text as a registration quotation.

violations.quote_as_written: The registered wording "chi2/7" is read as naming the raw dof=7 statistic, which is the one used for the gate decision.
violations.finding: 'chi2/7' is not a contiguous substring of registration.json (the field reads 'mean of chi2(rho_bin, C)/7 must lie in [0.8, 1.2]'). This is a shorthand paraphrase presented in quotation marks as 'the registered wording'.
violations.consequence: Minor; the interpretive point made (which of two candidate gate statistics the registered text names) is reasonable and is disclosed as an interpretation, not hidden, but the quote marks overstate its verbatim status.

violations.rule: Ground rule 12 (reproducibility) / internal consistency of a committed file
violations.finding: REPORT.md states as a disclosed 'Deviation': "the registered `seeds` field names the randoms seed 20260920; this run's `x2_lib.SEEDS["randoms"]` is 20260919 (matching the seed already fixed in `data/real2/cosmic_web/make_random_catalogue.py`...)". This is backwards from the committed code: `audit/reverse_zero_r2/X2-cosmic-web/x2_lib.py:36` sets `SEEDS = dict(..., randoms=20260920, ...)`, and line 175 uses `np.random.default_rng(SEEDS["randoms"])` -- i.e. the code actually uses 20260920, matching the registration exactly, and 20260919 (the value in make_random_catalogue.py, a separate, unrelated CSV-generation script not invoked by x2_lib.Ctx) does not appear anywhere in the X2-cosmic-web pipeline code. registration.json's own text (tests.X2.data.randoms) is explicit that 20260920 is 'a new seed; the existing file, seed 20260919, is not used for the primary' -- i.e. registration pre-emptively rules out exactly the substitution REPORT.md claims happened.
violations.consequence: Either (a) REPORT.md is stale documentation from an earlier code state and no seed deviation actually occurred (the more likely reading, since the code matches the registered value), in which case the disclosed 'effect: shifts the common noise floor but does not bias the data-vs-mock comparison' is moot and unnecessary, or (b) there is an unlocated code path that overrides SEEDS['randoms'] to 20260919 at runtime, which I did not find in x2_run.py, x2_lib.py, x2_fit_bias.py or x2_analyze.py (no CLI seed override exists). I could not find evidence for (b). This is reported as a documentation/reproducibility defect: the committed REPORT.md's own account of its pipeline's seed does not match the committed code that ran it, and the direction of the described mismatch is factually reversed from registration.json.
violations.note: Not one of the ground-rule-7 quote violations above (no quotation marks around invented text here) -- flagged separately as an accuracy defect in the committed record.

summary: Three genuine ground-rule-7 quotation defects (V1 high, V2 medium, V4 low) plus one 'invented-registration-phrasing' defect (V3, high) were found in the hand-written Markdown of X3-pta/README.md and X4-bao-cmb-sn/X4_RESULT.md -- none in the machine-generated quotes_verbatim JSON blocks, which is exactly where round 1's defect class would recur if it recurred: free-form prose, not the scripted grep-assert path. A fifth issue (V5) is a factual mismatch between X2-cosmic-web/REPORT.md's self-described seed deviation and the actual committed x2_lib.py code (the code uses the registered seed 20260920; the report claims 20260919 was used instead, backwards from what registration.json permits). None of the five findings changes any experiment's headline verdict (X1: WMAP null not rejected p_corr=0.472, SMICA anomaly p_corr=0.004; X2: INCONCLUSIVE, gate calibration fails; X3: CONDITIONAL, no unconditional bound; X4: informational for P1, CPL-vs-Lambda ~2.1-2.2 sigma) -- all four verdicts are independently reproduced from the committed numeric JSON and stand. Framing rules 5, 8, 9, 10, 11 are otherwise respected cleanly across all four experiments: no K3xT2-predicts language, both P1s consistently distinguished and named, 'pre-registered' never misused, DR2 never given a P1 verdict, and no upgrading of 'not rejected' into 'confirms'.
